references.text: The original formulation of the commandment against stealing in the Ten Commandments, as repeated in Deuteronomy 5:19.
Expands on the prohibition against stealing and links it to other ethical commands regarding honesty.
Prohibits extortion and robbery, which are related to the commandment against theft.
Mentions theft and its consequences in wisdom literature.
The prophet Jeremiah accuses the people of breaking the commandment against stealing along with other commandments.
Zechariah describes a curse that strikes thieves, linked to violating this commandment.
Jesus quotes the commandment against stealing when speaking with the rich young man.
Jesus mentions the commandment against stealing in his conversation about eternal life.
Luke's account where Jesus refers to the commandment against stealing.
Paul summarizes the commandments, including the prohibition against stealing, under the command of love.
Paul urges that whoever stole should stop stealing and instead work honestly.
